hypothesis: The exact symmetry-reduced scope-111 DTS CNF may contain a target witness that Kissat cannot reach within 120 seconds but can reach under a materially extended 1200-second single-process budget.
rationale: The prior sequential-counter encoding reduced the exact formula to 1,610,283 clauses and used 332 MB peak memory, but returned UNKNOWN at 119.64 solver seconds without producing a model. A tenfold solver budget is the narrowest remaining executable test of whether the prior result was a pure time-to-first-model effect; the mathematical instance and all exact constraints remain unchanged.
expected_information_gain: A SAT model independently accepted at scope<=111 would be true-objective progress. UNSAT would certify the finite frozen scope-111 instance. UNKNOWN after 1200 seconds would close this exact sequential-counter encoding at a materially extended budget, without implying mathematical infeasibility and without justifying another runtime-only repeat.
method: Generate the preserved DIMACS CNF for seven normalized six-mark rows with positive marks one-hot in 1..111, exact Sinz sequential at-most-one constraints for mark and difference-occurrence families, strict within-row order, complete lexicographic ordering of all five positive marks between adjacent rows, and per-row reflection symmetry a1+a4<=a5. Run Kissat 4.0.3 under WSL2 Ubuntu with a 1200-second solver limit. Decode any SAT model using the preserved mark-variable IDs and validate it with both repository integer verifiers, including the independent flat-counter check.
metric: SAT status, exact formula dimensions and hashes, solver elapsed time, decoded rows, and dual-verifier DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A decoded assignment accepted by both independent integer verifiers with scope<=111 is exactly true-objective progress. UNSAT is finite-instance evidence only; UNKNOWN or timeout is solver-budget evidence only.

configuration.encoding: one-hot marks plus explicit difference-occurrence auxiliaries and Sinz sequential at-most-one
configuration.symmetry_break: complete row lexicographic order plus per-row reflection a1+a4<=a5

kill_condition: Stop at SAT, UNSAT, or the 1200-second Kissat limit plus bounded process cleanup. Do not infer mathematical infeasibility from UNKNOWN or timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if a decoded model passes both independent verifiers

previous_best_comparison.sequential_short: UNKNOWN after 119.64 solver seconds on the same exact encoding
previous_best_comparison.symmetry_short: UNKNOWN after 119.34 solver seconds on the same finite decision problem with pairwise AMO
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: same exact finite decision problem; only the solver budget is extended tenfold

interpretation: Kissat returned UNKNOWN after the full 1200-second declared limit on the exact sequential-counter formula. No model was emitted, so the target was not reached and no mathematical infeasibility follows.
failure_mode: The exact sequential-counter encoding remained unresolved after a tenfold extension of the prior solver budget; this is a solver-budget result, not an UNSAT certificate.
what_was_learned: The same 30964-variable and 1610283-clause formula survived 1199.45 solver seconds and 332 MB peak resident memory without SAT or UNSAT. Compared with the prior 119.64-second UNKNOWN, extending the budget by 10x did not produce a witness or a finite infeasibility certificate. Both independent verifiers rejected the empty decode. This closes this exact sequential-counter encoding for the available CPU-only route at the tested budget.
recommended_next_action: Do not repeat this encoding with another runtime-only budget. Reallocate only to a materially different structural construction or exact-search capability; do not infer mathematical infeasibility from UNKNOWN.
repetition_justification: This repeats the same exact sequential-counter encoding only because the previous run ended at its 120-second kill condition without a solver conclusion. The declared 1200-second budget is a tenfold extension intended to test time-to-first-model, and it is explicitly the final runtime-only attempt for this encoding.
